summary: Unexpected 'Warmstart optimization premium' line on monthly invoice — explanation and credit request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CartoScale Inc. invoices contain a new line item labeled 'Warmstart optimization premium' for multiple hourly windows during February billing cycle. Customer says they did not opt into any premium feature and their reserved dedicated pool should be covered by their contract rate.

Impact:
- Unexpected charge ~ $1,230 on February invoice line items.
- Customer asks for immediate provisional credit and explanation.
- Affects finance reconciliation at month close.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity pool: cartoscale-prod-dedicated (us-west-2)
- Contract: Annual reserved capacity (4x A100 equivalent), billing tier enterprise-annual-2025
- Observed on finalized invoice INV-2026-02-789 (PDF snippet attached by customer)

Steps to reproduce (what customer did):
1) Customer ran normal production workload in us-west-2 during Feb 2–6 and Feb 18–19.
2) They viewed invoice and noticed multiple small warmstart premium line items aggregated to $1,230.
3) Opened support ticket requesting clarification and credit.

Expected behavior:
- No warmstart premium charges should apply to committed reserved capacity hours under enterprise-annual-2025 contract.

Actual behavior:
- System generated a per-hour surcharge labelled 'Warmstart optimization premium' for certain warmup windows during dedicated autoscaling events and a few scheduled warm-cache maintenance tasks.

Invoice snippet (customer-provided):
- 2026-02-03 02:00 UTC — Warmstart optimization premium — $210.00
- 2026-02-18 19:00 UTC — Warmstart optimization premium — $320.00
- 2026-02-19 03:00 UTC — Warmstart optimization premium — $700.00

Attachments provided by customer: invoice PDF page (redacted), timestamped job IDs, sample request IDs.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Maya Patel (Support): Received customer invoice and attachments, escalated to Billing + SRE. Provisional credit requested; awaiting internal confirmation.
2026-03-10 — Liam Chen (Billing): Acknowledged. Created internal INT-9001 for pricing-tag audit. Requested sample logs and pool identifiers from customer.

2026-03-11 — CartoScale (Customer): Uploaded invoice PDF and list of job IDs spanning suspected windows. Confirms reserved capacity should cover these hours per contract. Requests full reversal if error confirmed.

2026-03-11 — SRE (internal): Found warm-cache maintenance jobs initiated by autoscaler at 2026-02-18 19:00 and 2026-02-19 03:00. Labels on metrics pipeline show a new pricing_tag 'warmstart_premium' on those windows. Investigating origin of tag.

2026-03-12 — Liam Chen (Billing): Applied provisional credit of $1,230 to CartoScale account pending root cause analysis. Notified customer and created invoice memo detailing provisional credit reference CR-2026-03-110555.

2026-03-12 — Maya Patel (Support): Notified customer that provisional credit applied and that billing will remove charged lines post-confirmation. Customer requested confirmation email when final invoice is adjusted.
investigation: Query run: SELECT tags, job_id, start_ts, billing_tag FROM scheduler_job_events WHERE pool = 'cartoscale-prod-dedicated' AND start_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-02' AND '2026-02-20' — returned three warm-cache maintenance jobs with billing_tag='warmstart_premium'

Hypothesis 1: A recent autoscaler release (PR #4821) introduced optional warmstart optimization. During rollout the feature defaulted to 'on' for certain dedicated pools; billing system treated it as billable add-on and applied 'warmstart_premium' tag to job events.

Hypothesis 2: Contract override logic for enterprise-annual customers failed to match pricing_tag when job events included both 'reserved_hour' and 'warmstart_premium' flags; reserved-hours discount pipeline dropped and surcharge remained.

Cross-checks: Looked at contract pricing rules for enterprise-annual-2025 — confirmed policy explicitly waives warmstart surcharges for committed reserved hours, but billing service only sees 'reserved' tag when job attribution pipeline runs; race condition found between tag enrichment and pricing rule evaluation.

Findings: Race condition introduced in scheduler tagging enrichment after deploy of PR #4821 led to transient windows where scheduler emitted warmstart_premium before reserved_tag enrichment completed. Downstream pricing engine evaluated tag set without reserved_tag and applied surcharge.
resolution:
Root cause: rollout of warmstart optimization feature (PR #4821) inadvertently changed tag ordering for scheduler job events causing a short race window where 'warmstart_premium' was visible to billing without the 'reserved' attribution. Fix deployed: reorder enrichment so reserved attribution happens before any optional premium tags and added a guard in pricing evaluator to consider historical reserved contracts for matching pools.

Action taken:
- Provisional credit of $1,230 applied 2026-03-12 (CR-2026-03-110555).
- Billing team to regenerate adjusted invoice and issue corrected INV-2026-02-789-rev1 by 2026-03-15.
- Scheduler team rolled back the tag-order change and shipped fix (hotfix release 2026.03.12-hotfix-7).
- Added unit and integration tests to prevent tag-evaluation race; created INT-9001 for postmortem and follow-ups.

Customer follow-up: CartoScale confirmed provisional credit acceptance and asked for confirmation when finalized invoice is posted. Billing will email finalization and include memo referencing CR-2026-03-110555. Ticket closed after invoice revision posted.
public_resolution_note: We identified a tagging/order race introduced during a warmstart optimization rollout that caused short windows where a billable 'warmstart premium' tag wasn't paired with the reserved-hours contract attribution. We applied a provisional credit and issued a corrected invoice. Engineering has shipped a hotfix to prevent recurrence and added tests. If you see any further unexpected invoice lines, please reopen or open a new ticket.
